Set 1.q: 36. Which branch of geography presents dualism?
Set 1.explanation:
(c) : Regional and Systematic Geography
represent dualism in geography. Humboldt significantly
contributed to systematic geography, which follows an
empirical and inductive approach, while regional
geography focuses on studying specific areas. Carl
Ritter, Gallois, Brunhes, Blache, and De Martonne
made crucial contributions to regional geography.

Set 1.q:
57. Aurora Australis pertaining to ionosphere are
related to which hemisphere/region?
Set 1.explanation:
(c) : Aurora Australis pertaining to ionosphere are
related to southern Hemisphere. Aurora literally means
'dawn' while 'borealis' and 'australis' means 'northen' and
'southern' respectively. Therefore, they are referred to as
"northern polar light" (aurora borealis) and "southern
polar lights" (aurora australis). In reality, auroras are
cosmic glowing lights formed due to magnetic storms
caused by waves of electrons emitted from the surface
of the sun. Auroras appear like strange multicolored
fireworks hanging in the polar sky. They are usually
visible around midnight.

Set 1.q: 85. The transfer of heat is called –
Set 1.explanation:
(a) : The transfer and movement of heat through
the molecules of a substance is called conduction. In
conduction, heat is transferred from one molecule to
another by direct contact. Heat transfer in conduction
occurs in two ways:

same object.
2.  From one object to another in contact with it.
The process of heat transfer through the movement of
fluid masses (liquids or gases) is called convection.

rain-shadow
areas
are

Set 2.explanation:
(c) : Rain-fed and rain-shadow regions are
characteristics of orographic rainfall. The windward
slope of a mountain, where warm, moist air ascends and
cools, is called the windward slope or rain-fed slope.

warms at a rate of 10°C per 1000 meters, increasing
dryness and reducing relative humidity. Consequently,
no rain occurs on this side, which is called the rain-
shadow region.

vertically on the equator throughout the year, the
highest recorded temperature is observed at 20° North
latitude in July.

Favorable conditions for both El Niño and La
Niña

Unfavorable conditions for both El Niño and
La Niña
Set 3.explanation:
(a) : The Southern Oscillation refers to a weather
pattern involving the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
•  Normally, when the atmospheric pressure is low over
the Indian Ocean, it is high over the Pacific Ocean.
•  Conversely, if the pressure is low over the Pacific, it
is high over the Indian Ocean.
•  The intensity of the Southern Oscillation is measured
by the difference in atmospheric pressure.
•  A positive index indicates lower winter pressure over
the Indian Ocean and higher pressure over the
Pacific, which signifies normal monsoon conditions.
•  A negative index is associated with higher winter
pressure over the Indian Ocean, weakening the
monsoon.
•  A negative Southern Oscillation Index is directly
linked to El Niño development

27. Which one of the following statements is

options:
The youthful stage has maximum entropy and
maximum energy.

The mature stage has minimum entropy and
minimum energy.

The old age stage has minimum entropy and
minimum energy.

The old age stage has maximum entropy and
minimum energy.
Set 3.explanation:
(d) : As a river transitions from the mature stage to
the old age stage, its general condition changes
significantly. Compared to the mature stage, the number
of tributaries decreases, but remains higher than in the
youthful stage. Lateral erosion is dominant. Down
cutting completely ceases. Lakes and swamps appear on
the floodplains. Due to a significant decrease in river
velocity, its transport capacity reduces. Conversely, the
river's load is excessive in this stage. Consequently, the
river cannot transport its entire load, leading to increased
deposition. This state of a wide, slow-moving river with
extensive floodplains and deposition represents high
entropy and low available energy for work.

divided the known Earth into five zones: one torrid
zone, two temperate zones, and two frigid zones.
He was the first scholar to use a gnomon to measure the
correct length of the equator and estimated the Earth's
circumference to be 25,000 miles (actual: 25,860 miles).

distances of the Sun and Moon from the Earth.

geographical knowledge include Thales, Anaximander,
Hecataeus, Aristotle, Theophrastus, Polybius, and
Posidonius.

Set 4.q:
58. The condition when lapse rate of air is greater
than the dry adiabatic rate of cooling is called?
Set 4.explanation:
(b) : When the lapse rate of air is greater than the dry
adiabatic lapse rate, this condition is called absolute
instability. When warm, light air rises upward from the
surface and the normal lapse rate is greater than the dry
adiabatic lapse rate, the air continues to rise by itself
because it remains warmer than the surrounding air, and
thus becomes unstable with unstable equilibrium. Once the
air is saturated, its cooling rate decreases as it rises, and
since it remains warmer than the surrounding air, it
continues to ascend, creating permanent instability.
Atmospheric instability occurs when the cooling rate of
rising air (i.e., the dry adiabatic lapse rate) is less than the
normal lapse rate; in this case, the rising air remains
warmer than the surrounding air and keeps rising. As a
result, atmospheric instability persists. After condensation
at a certain height, if the rising air is still warmer than the
surrounding air-meaning, even after condensation, if the
moist adiabatic lapse rate is less than the normal lapse rate-
then the air continues to rise further. This type of
atmospheric instability is called absolute instability.

mountainous regions.

41. In which of the following states is laterite soil

lakh square kilometers in India. It is found on the
summits of the Sahyadri, Eastern Ghats, Rajmahal Hills,

Set 9.q:
46. The blueness of the sky is the result of
__________.
Set 9.explanation:
(d) : The sky appears blue due to scattering. Blue
light has the shortest wavelength in visible light, while red
has the longest. Therefore, blue light scatters much more
than red light. This scattering, known as Rayleigh
scattering, makes the sky appear blue.

Set 9.explanation:
(b) : Yardangs are formed by wind, not glaciers.
They are formed when layers of soft and hard rock are
found vertically aligned. Wind erodes the softer rock
more quickly than the hard rock and carries it away.
Thus, parts of the hard rock remain standing between
the eroded sections of soft rock. Wind erosion on the
sides of these rocks creates grooves. Such landforms are
called yardangs.

insolation. The amount of insolation received on the
surface varies from 320 watt/sqm in the tropics to 70
watt/sqm at the poles.
•  Outside the Tropic of cancer and the Tropic of
Capricorn, the slant of sunrays increases with the
increase in latitude, and the angle made by the rays
with the surface gradually becomes smaller. Thus, it

Set 9.q:
51. What is the name given to tropical cyclones in
Philippines.
Set 9.explanation:
(d) : In the Philippines, tropical cyclones are
known as Baguio. Tropical cyclones originate in the
intertropical convergence zone between 30° North and
30° South latitudes. They are low-pressure convergent
circulation systems, with an average diameter of up to
640 km. Their wind circulation is counterclockwise in
the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern
Hemisphere. Tropical cyclones are known by different
names in different regions:
• In the North Atlantic Ocean, particularly the
Caribbean Sea and southeastern USA → Hurricane
•  In the North Pacific Ocean, especially the China Sea,
eastern and southern coastal China, and Southeast
Asia → Typhoon
•  In Bangladesh and India’s eastern coastal regions →
Cyclone
•  In Australia → Willy-Willy.

(3) Secondary consumers (Carnivores)

Set 9.q: 90. River capture is more likely to occur when -
options:
The slope gradient is the same on both sides
of a water divide

There is a significant difference in the slope
gradient on both sides of a water divide.
Set 9.explanation:
(d) : When a main river or its tributary captures
the water of another river or its tributary, this
phenomenon is called river capture. The capturing river
is called the 'captor stream', and the river whose water is
captured is called the 'captured stream'. River capture
activities are more common in the youthful stage and
occur under the following conditions: The river slope is
steep (high slope gradient), the valley width is narrow,
the volume of water is large, the flow velocity is high
along with a steep slope, the river flows through weak
rock, the river's position is lower relative to others, and
the river carries less sediment load. A significant
difference in gradient across a divide encourages the
more aggressive river (steeper gradient, lower base
level) to erode headward and capture the other.

Earth's surface. This process of falling droplets of water
or ice is called precipitation. Precipitation can occur in
the form of water, solid ice, or a mixture of both, known

have a diameter of up to 5.50 mm. When the
temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into hail.

Ocean and in the western Pacific Ocean.

main cause of the collapse of the solar nebula was
gravitational attraction. The hypothesis is based on
Newton’s law of gravitation. Initially, the primordial
matter was spread out as cold, motionless, solid

Jadel (Scandinavia) etc.

Set 12.q:
15. At which of the following latitudes is the
smallest change in temperature of oceanic
water is observed with increasing depth?
Set 12.explanation:
(a) : North Pole
The smallest change in temperature of oceanic water
with increasing depth is observed at the North Pole.
This is because polar regions, particularly the North
Pole, have consistently cold surface waters due to the
presence of ice and low solar radiation. As a result, the
temperature gradient (thermocline) with depth is
minimal compared to lower latitudes, where surface
waters are warmer and exhibit a more pronounced
temperature drop with depth.

Set 13.q:

average of Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
was 34°C. If the temperature on Tuesday is 30°
C, then temperature on Friday was :
Set 13.explanation:
(d) : Average temp of Tuesday, Wednesday and
Thursday = 32°C
Total temp = 3 × 32°C
= 96°C
Average temp of Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
= 34°C
Total temp = 3×34°C
= 102°C
Temp on Tuesday = 30°C
⇒ Temp on (Wednesday + Thursday + Friday) –
(Tuesday + Wednesday + Thursday)
= 102°C – 96°C
Friday – Tuesday = 6°C
Friday = 6°C + Tuesday = 6°C + 30°C
Temp. on Friday = 36°C

Set 14.q:
6. Who is called the first geomorphologist in
North America?
Set 14.explanation:
(a) : G.K. Gilbert is considered to be the first
geomorphologist in North America. The word Pediment
was first used by G.K. Gilbert. He said that the process
of erosion of rocks to form a flat land and the process of
covering the surface with sediment is called leveling.
The Bonneville monograph (1890) was regarded as his
magnum opus. His report on the geology of the Henry
mountains (1877), in which the intrusive igneous
structure known as a loccolith was first described and
his history of the Niagara River (1890) were of
particular importance. G.K. Gilbert played an important
role

of

geological

Nomenclature and cartography.

Set 15.q:
6. Which of the following is not associated with
the structure of a tropical cyclone?
Set 15.explanation:
(d) : The Ekman spiral is not related to the
structure of a tropical cyclone, whereas the eye wall,
spiral band, and annular band are. Cyclones that form in
tropical regions (between 30°N - 30°S latitudes) are
called tropical cyclones. These are low-pressure
convergent circulation systems, with an average
diameter of up to 640 km.
The Ekman spiral refers to the deviation or deflection of
ocean currents due to wind forces. According to
Ekman’s theory, the movement of ocean surface water
driven by wind deflects 45° to the right in the
Northern Hemisphere and 45° to the left in the
Southern Hemisphere. The velocity of water flow
decreases with increasing depth due to reduced friction,
leading to the formation of spiral currents, known as
the Ekman spiral.

Set 15.q: 7. Which of the following statements is true?

The mantle-core boundary is determined by

The mantle-crust boundary is determined by
the Gutenberg discontinuity.

The mantle is primarily composed of iron and
nickel.
Set 15.explanation:
(a) : The velocity of seismic waves suddenly
increases at the base of the earth's crust. As wave travel
deeper into the Earth, pressure increases, leading to denser
and stiffer rock, which allows seismic waves to travel. The
Moho discontinuity marks the boundary between the
Earth's crust and mantle, while the Gutenberg discontinuity
marks the mantle-core boundary. The mantle is mainly
composed of silica and magnesium.

Set 15.q:
52. In which type of rock formations are almost all
of India's petroleum deposits found?
Set 15.explanation:
(d) : Almost all of India's petroleum deposits are
found in Tertiary sedimentary formations. Petroleum is
formed from the deposits of vegetation, but only from
plants that lack wood. Thick tree trunks and wooden
deposits primarily lead to the formation of coal. Since
vegetation did not exist during the first sedimentary deposit
formations, petroleum is only found in sedimentary rocks.
It is stored in sandstone or limestone in a manner similar to
how water is stored in a sponge. Over millions of years, the
decay of aquatic vegetation under heat and pressure led to
the formation of petroleum.

Set 16.q:
8. The fastest and deepest geostrophic currents are
found at the____boundaries of ocean basins.
Set 16.explanation:
(d) : The Earth rotates from west to east around its
axis. Due to this motion, water bodies cannot fully keep
up and lag behind, resulting in water movement from
east to west. This is why the fastest and deepest oceanic
currents are observed along western ocean coasts.
Ocean currents are of two types: (1) Cold currents, (2)
Warm currents. Currents flowing from the poles toward
the equator are cold currents, while currents flowing
from the equator toward the poles are warm currents.

correlation
between tension in life and number of
children.
C. Malthus based his theory of population on
experience of east European countries
D. Malthus positive checks include wars,
diseases, droughts, poverty etc.
E. The unchecked population increases at
arithmetic rate while subsistence (food)
increases at geometric rate
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below.
Set 17.explanation:
(d) : Thomas Robert Malthus was the first thinker
who systematically propounded a theory on the
relationship between population and resources. He
traveled across Britain and several Western European
countries to collect statistical data and presented his
population theory in a scientific form.
Malthus’ population theory is based on the following
key ideas:
● Geometric Increase of Population – According to
Malthus, population grows in a geometric (exponential)
ratio (1:2:4:8:16 …). In the absence of checks (natural
or artificial), population doubles every 25 years.
●  Arithmetic Increase of Food Supply – According to
him, food supply increases slowly in an arithmetic
ratio (1, 2, 3, 4 …). Due to the law of diminishing
returns in agriculture, food production eventually
shows declining growth.
●  Imbalance between Population and Food Supply –
Because population grows faster than food supply, an
increasing gap arises between them, leading to
imbalance between population and means of
subsistence.
●  Checks on Population Growth – Malthus believed that
population growth could be checked in two ways:
 Natural checks: epidemics, famines, wars, floods,
earthquakes, etc.
 Preventive (artificial) checks: self-control, celibacy,
late marriages, or not marrying at all.
Hence, statements (A), (C), and (E) are incorrect.

Set 18.explanation:

nations in resource production but also by other factors,
including the unequal distribution of resources between

technological
advancements
in
resource
extraction, climate change policies, etc. The distribution
of natural resources is not uniform but rather
concentrated in certain areas. Hence, some regions are
resource-rich while others are poor or resource-

internal resources. The tendency of a state’s industrial
and technological development largely depends on the
management and efficient utilization of its natural
resources. Proper management, use, and technological
development of resources enable a state to impose or
enforce its will/decisions on others.

of a river cycle

surface
formed
by
merging
floodplains

of erosion

Set 20.explanation:
(a) : Only (A) and (E)
The term 'Peneplain' refers to a flat surface formed in
the old age stage of the river cycle, and as the ultimate
product of erosion. The concept of the geographic cycle

It affects the direction of the wind.

Its magnitude is determined by the speed of
the wind.
It is maximum at the poles.
Set 20.explanation:
(a) : The Coriolis force is a deflective force caused
by the Earth's rotation, which influences the direction of
the wind. Due to this force, winds turn to the right in the
Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern
Hemisphere. In the absence of the Coriolis force, winds
would always move directly from high-pressure to low-
pressure areas across isobars. The Coriolis force does
not affect the speed of the wind.

used "Ethology" in 1859, and British naturalist Mivart
coined "Hexicology" for similar studies.

Set 21.explanation:

absence of major river inflows contribute to high
salinity in these regions.

horizontal movement and compression, it is called a
nappe. The Kashmir Valley in India is located on a
nappe.

60. The concept of "Stop-and-Go Determinism"

Set 21.explanation:
(a) : G. Taylor proposed "Stop-and-Go
Determinism," which suggests that nature does not
have absolute control over humans, but its influence
cannot be denied. Canadian geographer George
Tatham referred to Taylor’s ideology as "Pragmatic
Possibilism." According to Tatham, Taylor used more
restrained terminology, replacing "control" with
"influence" and "influence" with "response" or
"adjustment."

Set 22.q:
32. The force that generates tides is the difference
between which of the following two forces?
Set 22.explanation:
(c) : Gravitational pull and centrifugal force
Explanation: The force responsible for generating tides
is the difference between gravitational pull and
centrifugal force.
The gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun
attracts ocean water, while the centrifugal force due to
Earth's rotation pushes the water outward, creating
tides.
Tides do not occur at the same time every day. Instead,
each tide arrives 26 minutes later than the previous
day. This means that the second tide occurs
approximately 12 hours and 26 minutes after the
first tide.
As the Earth rotates from west to east, the tidal bulges
move from east to west.

Set 22.q:
33. The Benioff zone is found along which type of
plate boundaries?
Set 22.explanation:
(b) : Destructive plate boundaries – A rigid
landmass is called a plate. The study of the nature and
movement of these plates is known as plate tectonics.
The plate tectonics theory was introduced by Harry
Hess in 1960, but its scientific explanation is credited to
W.J. Morgan.
The Benioff zone is found along destructive plate
boundaries. When two plates collide, the denser plate
subducts beneath the less dense plate. The region where
the plate sinks is called the subduction zone. Since the
plate is being destroyed in this area, it is called a
destructive plate boundary.

death rates, five stages of demographic transition
are more clearly defined:
1.  First stage – High stationary: Both birth and
death rates are high.
2.  Second stage – Early expanding: The birth rate
remains high, but the death rate declines.
3.  Third stage – Late expanding: Both birth and
death rates decline.
4.  Fourth stage – Low stationary: Both birth and
death rates stabilize at a low level.
5.  Fifth stage (proposed later) – Population decline
begins.

Set 23.q: 50. Who first used the term "Geography"?
Set 23.explanation:
(c) : The term "Geography" was first used by
Eratosthenes in Greece. He attempted to establish
geography as a distinct field of study. Eratosthenes
divided the known Earth into five zones: one torrid
zone, two temperate zones, and two frigid zones.
He was the first scholar to use a gnomon to measure the
correct length of the equator and estimated the Earth's
circumference to be 25,000 miles (actual: 25,860 miles).
In his book, he referred to the habitable world as
"Oikoumene." He also attempted to measure the
distances of the Sun and Moon from the Earth.
Other Greek scholars who contributed significantly to
geographical knowledge include Thales, Anaximander,
Hecataeus, Aristotle, Theophrastus, Polybius, and
Posidonius.

Set 23.q:
51. During which phase of the Moon does a neap
tide occur?
Set 23.explanation:
(a) : Explanation:
Neap tides occur during the first and third quarter
phases of the Moon. During these phases, on the
seventh or eighth day of the waxing (Shukla Paksha)
and waning (Krishna Paksha) lunar cycles, the Sun,
Earth, and Moon form a right angle. As a result, the
tidal forces of the Moon and the Sun counteract each
other, leading to lower-than-average tides, known as
neap tides.
Neap tides are 20% lower than normal tides.
Spring tides, which occur during New Moon and Full
Moon, are 20% higher than normal tides.

Set 24.q:
17. Which of the following statements about

significantly affect the weather conditions
of the impacted regions.

known as 'Foehn.'

Eaters' because they cause a sudden rise in
temperature, leading to the melting of
surface snow.

descend along mountain slopes in the U.S. They
primarily blow from Colorado to British Columbia,
Canada, along the eastern slopes of the Rocky
Mountains. These winds are also known as 'Snow
Eaters' because they cause a sudden temperature rise,
sometimes increasing by 34°F in just minutes, leading
to rapid snowmelt. This makes them beneficial for
livestock farmers as they help clear pastures.

Set 24.q: 19. The Dead Sea is a lake formed by ___________.
Set 24.explanation:

valley. It is an important example of a rift valley, with
its bottom approximately 2,500 feet below sea level.
When two normal faults extend for several kilometers in
such a way that the land between them sinks, the
resulting landform is called a rift valley. The Dead Sea
is located between Jordan and Israel.

Set 24.q:
29. Which of the following statements are correct
about fold mountains?
1. They are formed under the influence of
compressional tectonic forces.
2. Deep gorges and pyramidal peaks are
formed in fold mountains.
3. Igneous sedimentary and metamorphic
rocks are found in mountain region.
options: More than one of the above
Set 24.explanation:
(d) : Fold mountains are formed due to
Compressional tectonic forces, where two tectonic
plates collide. This causes the Earth's crust to crumple
and fold, forming mountain ranges. The Himalayas and
the Alps are the examples of fold mountains.
•  Deep gorges and pyramidal peaks often develop in
fold mountains due to long-term processes such as
erosion and glaciation.
•  Fold mountain regions contain a mix of igneous,
sedementary, and metamorphic rocks.

western parts of continents between 30° and 40°
latitudes on both sides of the equator. This climate

70. How does climate change effect habitat
suitability for species?
options:
Alters temperature and precipitation patterns,
affecting habitat availability
Reduces the need for species migration
Enhances habitat conditions for all species
More than one of the above
Set 24.explanation:

alters temperature and rainfall patterns, which impacts
habitat availability. The effects of climate change are

wind and rainfall, influencing the

Set 24.q:
75. What theory explains the movement of earth's
lithosphere plates?
options: More than one of the above
Set 24.explanation:
(a) : The outer part of the Earth is made up of
solid landmasses called plates. The study of the nature
and movement of these plates is called plate tectonics.
A tectonic plate is a large, irregular block of solid rock
composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere.
These plates move horizontally as rigid units over the
asthenosphere. Thus, the theory of plate tectonics
explains the movement of lithospheric plates of the
Earth.

Set 25.q:
77. Who proposed the "Subsistence Theory"
related to population theories?
Set 25.explanation:
(d) : The "Subsistence Theory" was proposed by
David Ricardo.
David Ricardo accepted Malthus' theory but took a
critical approach. He developed his theory based on
the normative model of the market system. According
to him, labor is a commodity like any other in a market
economy. He argued that humans are rational
economic beings who respond to market trends.
When labor demand increases, wages rise, leading to
higher population growth and an increased labor
supply. As a result, wages eventually decrease.
Ultimately, wages stabilize at the subsistence level.
According to Ricardo, wage levels primarily depend
on labor supply (population growth) and capital
accumulation. In such a system, a balanced state is
eventually achieved. When labor demand and supply are
equal, no further capital accumulation occurs, leading to
the application of the law of diminishing returns.
Like Malthus, Ricardo also believed that poverty and
misery are natural inevitabilities.

Set 27.q:
9. Who among the following was a key figure in
Quantitative Revolution in Geography?
Set 27.explanation:
(b) : The key figure behind the quantitative
revolution in geography was Peter Haggett. His 1965
book Locational Analysis in Human Geography is
considered a landmark work in quantitative geography.
He made extensive use of mathematical and statistical
methods in geographical analysis and research. During
this period, geography increasingly emphasized the use
of mathematics and statistics for explaining and
generalizing spatial facts based on direct observation
and for model building. This transformative shift in
geographical thought is known as the Quantitative
Revolution. The quantitative revolution in geography
began in the United States in the 1950s under the
leadership of Schaefer, Berry, and Garrison, and
reached its peak in the early 1960s. Halford Mackinder
is known as a political geographer, while Carl Sauer is
known as a cultural and historical geographer.

Set 28.q:
47. Generally, the interval between a spring tide
and a neap tide is ..........
Set 28.explanation:
(b) : 7 days
Explanation: Due to the gravitational pull of the Sun
and the Moon, the seawater rises and falls, a
phenomenon known as tides. When the Sun, Moon, and
Earth align in a straight line, which occurs on every full
moon and new moon, this alignment is called "syzygy".
During these days, spring tides occur, which are larger
tides.Such spring tides occur twice a month (on the new
moon and full moon). On the seventh and eighth days of
both the waxing (Shukla Paksha) and waning (Krishna
Paksha) phases of the lunar month, the Sun, Earth, and
Moon form a right angle. This positioning results in
neap tides, which are weaker tides.
Hydrosphere
373
YCT
Thus, we can conclude that spring tides occur on full
moon and new moon days, while neap tides occur on
the seventh and eighth lunar days of each phase (Shukla
Paksha and Krishna Paksha). Therefore, the interval
between a spring tide and a neap tide is generally 7
days.
Note: The interval between two consecutive tides is 24
hours and 52 minutes, whereas semi-diurnal tides occur
at intervals of 12 hours and 26 minutes.

is concerned with discovering those aspects which are
considered real and significant in social life from the
perspective of commonly accepted socioeconomic
categories.

the pioneer of this approach. According to him, the
Structuralism method can be applied to various fields

architecture.

Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Arhar, being a leguminous crop,
help in restoring soil fertility.
Reason (R)
: Arhar is mostly grown in
rotation with other crops.
choose the correct answer from the option
given below:
options:
(A) and (R) both are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A)

(A) and (R) both are true but (R) is not
correct explanation of (A)
Set 29.explanation:
(b) : • Assertion (A) : Arhar, being a leguminous
crop, helps in restaring soil fertility. Yes, Arhar (Pigeon
Pea) is a leguminous crop. Leguminous crops fix
atmospheric nitrogen into the soil through symbiotic
bacteria in their root nodules (Rhizobium).
This process enriches soil nitrogen and thus restores soil
fertility.
• Reason (R) : Arhar is mostly grown in rotation with
other crops.
Yes, Arhar is commonly grown in crop rotation
systems with Cereals and other crops. Crops rotation
helps in reducing pest buildup and maintaing soil
health.
• Does (R) explain (A) ?
No, while (R) is true, it does not explain why Arhar
restores soil fertility. Crop rotation is a farming
practice, but the reason Arhar restores soil fertility is
nitrogen fixation, which is unrelased to rotation.
Rotation is beneficial but not the cause of soil
fertility restoration by Arhar.

Set 30.q:
13. Which pressure belt is also called the Horse
Latitude?
Set 30.explanation:
(a) : The Subtropical High-Pressure Belt is found
between 30°–35° latitudes in both hemispheres. It acts
as a dividing zone between two opposing surface winds
(Trade Winds and Westerlies). The air rising at the
equator moves in the opposite direction of the trade
winds
and
descends
around
30°–35°
latitudes,
increasing the pressure and creating anticyclonic
conditions. This results in atmospheric stability and
reduced wind movement, with winds blowing in various
directions. In ancient times, ships loaded with horses
faced difficulties navigating this calm and uncertain
wind region, leading traders to throw some horses into
the sea to lighten their ships. This is why it is called the
"Horse Latitude."

Set 30.q: 77. Orographic rainfall is caused by

More than one of the above
Set 30.explanation:
(c) : Orographic rainfall on formed where air rises
and cools because of a topographic barrier. When their
temperature fall below dew point, clouds are formed.
These clouds cause widespread rain on the windward
slopes of the mountain range. This type of rain is known as
orographic rainfall. However when these winds cross over
the mountain range and descend along the leeward slopes,
they get warm and cause little rain. Region lying on the
leeward side of the mountain receiving little rain is called
rain shadow area. It is also known as the relief rain.
Hence, orographic rainfall is caused by lifting of air by
mountains or hills.

Set 30.explanation:

causes of earthquakes, was proposed by H.F. Reid. He
suggested that subsurface rocks behave like rubber and
stretch when pulled. As stress increases in elastic rocks,
it builds tension and strain. Once the limit of elasticity
is exceeded, rocks release accumulated energy, causing
earthquakes.

Lack of compatibility with remote sensing

Meteorological Department, a drought occurs when an

normal levels. Drought is a situation caused by
prolonged low rainfall, excessive evaporation, and
overexploitation of water reservoirs and groundwater,
leading to a shortage of surace water.

agriculture is—
Set 31.explanation:
(b) : In shifting cultivation, farmers frequently
change their fields and residences. The primary
characteristic of shifting agriculture is field rotation.
The major food crops include maize, sorghum, millet,
and rice. Farmers clear forests for cultivation, and after
a few years, they move to another location and repeat
the process. The yield in this type of agriculture is very
low. Hence, farmers also rely on hunting, forestry, and
gathering. In Assam, this practice is called Jhum, and in
Andhra Pradesh, it is called Podu.

rainfall affected by the Southern Oscillation?
Set 31.explanation:
(b) : The Southern Oscillation significantly
influences the monsoon. Its cycle typically lasts
between 2 to 5 or 7 years. Discovered by Walker in
1908, this concept describes an oscillating weather
pattern between the Pacific Ocean and the Indian
Ocean. When atmospheric pressure is high over the
Pacific Ocean, it is low over the Indian Ocean, and vice
versa. A lower pressure over the Indian Ocean
strengthens the southwest monsoon in India, whereas
higher pressure weakens it.

River erosion in the mature stage
River deposits in the old age stage

depression filled with water. When river meanders
become excessively curved, the river often cuts through
the neck of the meander and flows straight. The
abandoned meander loop fills with water, forming an
ox-bow lake. (Note: While deposition is involved in
sealing off the meander, the primary process leading to
the cutoff is lateral erosion in the mature stage).

A. Societies characterized by a low age at
marriage exhibit low fertility rate.

contribution to determining fertility. In male-dominated

Human and Settlement Geography

considered objects of pleasure, and are given a lower

30. Identify the correct statement from the

options:
Wind is deflected to its right in the southern
hemisphere

Geostrophic wind blows parallel to the
isobars

Wind speed is inversely proportional to
pressure gradient force
Set 32.explanation:
(b) : Geostrophic winds blows parallel to the
isobars. The rotation of the earth on its axis affects the
direction of winds. Due to the coriolis effect, the winds
are deflected to the right from their direction in northern
hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere.
Wind speed does not increase with friction. In fact, it
decreases. Wind speed is directly proportional to
pressure gradient force (PGF)-not inversely. The greater
the pressure gradient, the greater will be the velocity of
the winds and the more the direction of the winds will
be deflected.

Set 33.q:
88. Which of the following is commonly added to
solve the problem of soil salinity?
Set 33.explanation:
(a) : Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate-CaSO4.2H2O) is
commonly added to saline and sodic soils to improve
their structure and reduce salinity. In saline soils,
especially sodic soils with high sodium content, gypsum
provides calcium ions (Ca2+) that replace sodium ions
(Na+) on soil particles. This exchange helps to –
• Improve soil permeability.
• Enhance water infiltration.
• Reduce soil crusting and compaction.
Over time, this process leaches the displaced sodium
out of the root zone, thereby reclaining the soil and
making it more suitable for plant growth. Whereas
potash and phosphate do not contribute directly in soil
salinity. And Urea is added to fullfill Nitrogen
requirement.

solid (like ice) turns directly into a gas (water vapor)

rock transversed

density and resistance of rock transversed.

given below:
Set 34.explanation:

by compressing and expanding the material through
which they pass. They can travel through both solids
and liquids and move faster than S-waves.

seismic waves and follow a zig-zag path as they
move along the surface of earth.

material they are passing through, but it is not
affected by the resistance of rock transversed.

81. River valleys that initially flow in the same

reference to new base levels are known as—
Set 35.explanation:

direction as the original consequent drainage but later
develop at lower topographic levels concerning new
base levels are known as resequent valleys. Drainage
systems refer to the origin of rivers and their evolution
over time, whereas drainage patterns refer to the
geometric arrangement and spatial organization of
rivers in a given area.
Drainage systems are classified into two major types:
1.  Consequent drainage system – Rivers that
follow the slope of the land, including consequent,
subsequent, obsequent, and resequent rivers.
2. Insequent (Discordant)- A drainage pattern is
described as discordant if it does not correlate to
the topology and geology of the area.
It is further classified into two main types:
(i) Antecedent
(ii) Superimposed

Eurasia and North America.

Set 37.q: 56. Westerly winds are an example of what?
Set 37.explanation:
(a) : Westerly winds are macro-scale atmospheric
motions. These are permanent winds blowing between
the subtropical high-pressure belts (30° to 35°) and
subpolar low-pressure belts (60° to 65°) in both
hemispheres. In the Northern Hemisphere, they flow
from southwest to northeast, while in the Southern
Hemisphere, they flow from northwest to southeast. The
polar boundary of these winds fluctuates. When warm
and moist westerly winds meet the cold polar winds,
fronts are formed. Compared to trade winds, westerlies
are more complex. Therefore, in the Southern
Hemisphere, they are known as "Roaring Forties" (40°-
50° latitudes), "Furious Fifties" (near 50° latitude), and
"Screaming Sixties" (near 60° latitude).

Set 37.q:
67. ldentify the correct statements with reference
to Geomorphic Cycles of Davis and Penck.
A. Davis considered the cycle of erosion of
fluvial process as the 'normal cycle of
erosion'.
B. Davis used the concept of 'base level'
proposed by Gilbert and concept of
'graded streams' propounded by Powell
and applied 'evolutionary paradigm
C. In the second sub-phase of the phase of
uniform development of landscape of
Penck model absolute height increases and
relative relief also increases at the same
rate.
D. Davis applied the concept of slope decline.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
Set 37.explanation:
(b) : With reference to the geomorphic cycles of
Davis and Penck, the following statements are correct:
• Davis considered the fluvial process cycle as the
“normal cycle of erosion.”
• Davis introduced the concept of slope decline.
• In Penck’s model, during the second sub-stage of
uniform landscape development, there is no increase in
absolute elevation or relative relief because the rates of
summit decline and uplift are equal.
Davis did not apply Gilbert’s concept of base level or
Powell’s concept of graded rivers to his evolutionary
paradigm.
Powell (1875) proposed the concept of the “base level,”
where sea level represents the ultimate base below
which dry land cannot be eroded. Gilbert formulated the
“sixth power law,” which states that a river’s
transporting capacity is proportional to the sixth power
of its velocity. Gilbert emphasized quantitative analysis
over qualitative in landform and process studies, using
thermodynamic models.
Davis was the first to propose a real “general theory” of
landform development. His geomorphic theory is actually
a group of several theories, three major ones being:
1. The complete cycle of a river’s life,
2. The geographic cycle,
3. The cycle of slope development.
Davis observed the cyclic method of landform
development in a historical context, explaining that
landform creation and evolution are influenced by
structure, process, and time.

Set 38.q:
17. Which feature is commonly associated with
convergent plate boundaries?
options: More than one of the above
Set 38.explanation:
(a) : Deep-sea trenches are associated with
convergent plate boundaries. A destructive boundary
is called a convergent plate boundary. In this type, two
plates move toward each other and collide. The leading
edge of one plate (composed of relatively lighter
material) rides over the leading edge of the other plate
(composed of denser, heavier material). As a result, the
edge of the heavier plate is subducted into the mantle,
where it melts and is destroyed. The consequences of
such plate convergence, collision, and subduction
include:
explosive
volcanic
eruptions,
folded
mountains, island arcs and trenches, and the
formation of deep-sea trenches. Hence, option (a) is
correct

Set 39.q:
29. The horizontal air photos are also called as –––
––––
Set 39.explanation:
(d) : Horizontal aerial photographs are also called
terrestrial photographs. For taking horizontal or ground
(terrestrial) aerial photographs, the camera axis is
brought parallel to the horizontal plane. These
photographs provide only an elevation view. Horizontal
photographs can generally be taken with good cameras,
which are used as auxiliaries for the analysis of vertical
photographs. They are especially important in regional
studies, particularly in geological, forestry, and
geomorphological investigations. To take oblique
photographs, the camera axis in the aircraft is tilted
toward the ground. Such photographs show side views
of ground details. Aerial photographs taken with a tilted
camera axis are called oblique photographs. These
photographs cover a very large area on the ground, but
the accuracy and clarity of details decrease with
distance from the center. Oblique photography is
extremely important for strategic purposes. During
wartime, such aerial photographs are very useful for
detecting tanks, vehicles, supply depots, and arsenals
hidden under trees by the enemy. Trimetrogon means
"triple" or "three-way" operation. In this system, three
cameras are used simultaneously in a camera unit. The
central camera takes vertical ground photographs, while
the side cameras take oblique aerial photographs
extending to the horizon. Thus, in the triple system, the
entire area from the right horizon to the left horizon is
recorded.

Set 40.q:
23. The Concept of the Lowest (Base Level)
Erosion Was Introduced By:
Set 40.explanation:
(d) : In 1875, Powell proposed the concept of base
level. According to Powell, the sea level represents the
ultimate base level, below which dry land cannot
undergo erosion. However, for temporary and local
purposes, there can be additional base levels, usually
corresponding to the level of the main riverbed.
The base level is essentially an imaginary surface that
gradually slopes towards the lower course of the main
river.
There are three types of base levels:
1. Permanent Base Level (determined by sea level)
2. Temporary Base Level
3. Local Base Level
Note: Every river has a final limit for vertical
(downward) erosion, beyond which further erosion is
not possible. This limit is called the base level of a river
or the lowest level of erosion.

66. Given below are two statements, one is labelled
as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): J.T. Hack proposed the concept
of dynamic equilibrium in Geomorphology.
Reason (R): J.T. Hack did not emphasize that
landscape achieve a balance between tectonic
uplift and denudational process.

below:
Code -
options:

correct explanation of (A)

Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A)
Set 41.explanation:
(d) : J.T. Hack introduced the concept of dynamic
equilibrium in geomorphology. He emphasized that the
landscape achieves a balance between tectonic uplift
and denudation processes. The central reference
framework of Hack’s theory is that “a geomorphic
system is an open system that tends toward
equilibrium.” Hack’s model of landform development
can be expressed as:
“The form of landforms is based on the balance
(adjustment) between the resistance of available
structure to erosion and the erosional energy of
operative processes.”
Therefore, statement (A) is true but the reason (R) is
false.

Set 42.q:
82. Noctilucent clouds are found in which sphere of
the atmsophere?
Set 42.explanation:
(c) : In the mesosphere layer of the atmosphere,
noctilucent clouds are found. The mesosphere extends
from 50 to 80 km above sea level. These clouds are
observed over the poles during summer. They form
through the condensation caused by meteoric dust and
moisture brought upward by convective processes.
The lowest layer of the atmosphere is called the
troposphere or the "zone of change." The term
"troposphere" was coined by Léon Teisserenc de Bort.
The layer above the tropopause is called the
stratosphere. This layer was first discovered and studied
by Léon Teisserenc de Bort.
The ionosphere in the atmosphere extends from 80 km
to 640 km above sea level.

Set 44.q:

Set 44.explanation:

included among the centers around 1950 that
emphasized the well-defined theoretical aspects of
geography as a science of spatial analysis, whereas the
University of Iowa, the University of Wisconsin, and
the University of Washington were included. The
quantitative revolution in American geography began in
the mid-1950s under the leadership of Harold
McCarthy, Brian Berry, and Garrison. At the University
of Iowa, McCarthy tried to establish laws governing
geographic patterns. At the University of Wisconsin,
Professor Robins developed statistical methods for map
comparison. At the University of Washington in Seattle,

university, Professor Edward Ullman emphasized
geography as a science of functional inter-areal
relationships and made significant contributions to the
success of the quantitative revolution.

phosphorous and potassium. Due to this, it is not naturally
fertile and requires fertilizers for cultivation.

Set 44.q:
22. In contrast to Mackinder's Heart land Theory,
Spykman's Rimland Theory emphasies which
regions strategic importance?
Set 44.explanation:
(a) : Contrary to Mackinder’s Heartland Theory,
Spykman’s Rimland Theory emphasizes the strategic
importance of the coastal marginal areas of Eurasia.
In his book “The Geography of Peace”, Spykman
explained his concept of the Rimland or the Periphery.
He firmly believed that in contemporary world politics,
the basis of international strategic relations lies in
maritime power, not in the future possibilities of
Heartland development. Spykman’s Rimland included
continental Europe west of the Baltic and Black Sea
isthmus,
the
mountainous,
southwestern,
and
southeastern regions of Asia, and China. He criticized
Mackinder’s theory of Heartland dominance as flawed
and
put
forth
a
new
strategic
formula:
“Who controls the Rimland rules Eurasia; who rules
Eurasia controls the destinies of the world.”

Set 44.q:
69. Consider the correct statements regarding
possibilities of meander change over time.
A. Meanders may migrate upstream and erode
river cliffs
B. They may migrate laterally and erode the
flood plain
C. They may become exaggerated and become
ox-bow lake
D. Under special conditions they may become
intrenched or ingrow.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below.
Set 44.explanation:
(a) : Meanders can migrate laterally and erode the
floodplains. They can become exaggerated and take the
shape of ox-bow or oxbow lakes (ox-arch). Under
special circumstances, they can become intermittent.
They (meanders) cannot migrate upstream and erode the
steep rocks of the river. When an adult river enters the
plain, horizontal erosion is more active than downward
erosion. As a result, the river starts widening its valley
instead of deepening it. At this stage, the path of the
river is neither flat nor made of uniform rocks.
Therefore, rivers do not flow in a straight path but move
through a winding path. Due to this, small and big
bends are formed in the path of the river. These bends
are called river meanders. Hence, option (a) is correct.

regions can exist as there are subject elements in a

their mutual interrelationships. On this basis, regions

soil layers, enabling it to survive in arid and semi-

Set 46.q: 11. Katabatic wind is
Set 46.explanation:
(a) : Katabatic wind is a downhill wind. At night,
due to radiation, there is greater loss of heat on mountain
slopes and upper areas, which makes the air cold. This cold
and heavy air descends along the slopes into the valleys.
These are called mountain breezes or katabatic winds. Due
to these winds, temperature inversion occurs, which results
in frost or dew formation in valleys at night, while upper
regions remain frost-free.

geographical thought become "humanistic
geography"?
Set 46.explanation:
(b) : Antipode
Explanation: In 1969, the journal Antipode was
established at Clark University in Worcester. This research
journal published articles related to radical reformism. The
research papers in this journal addressed issues such as
urban poverty, discrimination against women, racial and
minority bias, unequal distribution of social services, and
crime. Hence, with the publication of Antipode in 1969,
humanistic geography became a major focus of
geographical thought.

a perspective that revealed the complexity and
ambiguity of the relationships between humans and
places, emphasizing human experiences and conditions.

(D) Abnormally stagnant winds

Set 46.explanation:

decreases with height, at a lapse rate of approximately

mixing, pollutants, dust, and smoke remain trapped near
the surface, leading to severe air quality issues.

development:

husbandry.
2. Polis: Transformation of large villages into small
towns; specialization grows.

rural areas.

population and prosperity.

trade, services.

importance almost lost.

Set 48.q:
67. Who among the following has included both
empirical and genetic classification in the world
climate classification?
Set 48.explanation:
(b) : In the classification of world climate, G.T.
Trewartha incorporated both empirical and genetic
classifications, whereas Koppen and Thornthwaite’s
classifications are empirical. Trewartha modified
Koppen’s system to develop his own, which combined
empirical (based on observation) and genetic (based on
causation) elements. His main objective was to simplify
classification so that only a few main climate types
could be identified across the globe. He did not favor a
large number of climate types. Like Koppen, he used
temperature and rainfall as the basis of classification.
He identified six primary climate types at the global
level, labeled as A, B, C, D, E, and H. Among these, the
"B" climate type was based on rainfall, while the others
were primarily based on temperature.

Set 50.q:
5. The extensive area between the continental
shelf and the abyssal plain is known as:
Set 50.explanation:
(c) : The steeply sloping zone between the
submerged shore and the deep oceanic plains is called
the continental slope. Notably, sediment deposition is
absent on the slopes due to their steep incline,
preventing debris from settling. The average slope is
between 2° and 5°, with depths ranging from 200
meters to 3000 meters. Continental slopes cover
approximately 8.5% of the total oceanic area, with the
greatest extension found in the Atlantic Ocean (12.4%).
Note: The edge of the slope marks the termination of
continents, where canyons and trenches are also found.

Blache and Reclus
Select the correct answer from the options

Set 50.explanation:
(d) : Vidal de la Blache, Lucien Febvre, and
Élisée Reclus criticized and opposed environmental
determinism.
French
geographers
contributed
significantly to possibilism, geographical unity,
regional studies, and cultural landscapes. They argued
that humans themselves are both the problem and the
solution, while nature is merely a guide. In contrast,
determinists believed that human activities are
controlled entirely by environmental conditions. This
ideology developed mainly in 19th and early 20th-
century Germany, with key proponents like Ratzel,
Ellen Churchill Semple, and Ellsworth Huntington.

Set 50.q:
23. The perspective in geography that states that
"actions are driven by cognitive processes" is
the essence of:
Set 50.explanation:
(c) : The perspective that "actions are driven by
cognitive processes" is the essence of behaviorism.
William Kirk made significant contributions to the early
development of behavioral geography.
The fundamental philosophy of behaviorism is rooted in
psychology or phenomenology, which considers a
purely value-neutral and objective study to be
incomplete and instead emphasizes human experience
and cognition. The main objective of behaviorism is to
develop a new approach based on human perception to
explain the relationship between humans and their
natural environment.
In behavioral geography, human behavior (conduct) is
considered
the
most
important
factor,
and
in
geographical analysis, human individual or collective
behavior is prioritized. The study of cultural elements in
a region takes into account human interest, skill,
awareness, and cognitive abilities. Thus, in behavioral
geography, human behavior is considered the most
significant factor.

Set 50.q:
30. If the earth were a solid part made of rocks of
the same density then.
options:
Seismic waves reached the earth's core in a
straight line at uneven speed.

Seismic waves reach the earth's core in a
straight line at the same speed

Seismic waves follow a curved path at uneven
speed

Seismic waves follow a carved path at
uniform speed
Set 50.explanation:
(b) : Seismic waves reach the earth's core in a
straight line at the same speed.
 If the earth had a uniform density throughout, the
velocity of P, S & L seismic waves would be
consistent at all depths, but because the earth's
composition changes significantly with depth, the
speed of these waves varies considerably as they
travel through different layer.
 The speed of seismic waves, particularly P and S
waves, is directly related to the density and elastic
properties of the material they are travelling
through.

Set 50.explanation:

introduced by Notestein in 1945.
•
According to the patterns of change in birth and
death rates, five stages of demographic transition
are more clearly defined:
1.  First stage – High stationary: Both birth and
death rates are high.
2.  Second stage – Early expanding: The birth rate
remains high, but the death rate declines.
3.  Third stage – Late expanding: Both birth and
death rates decline.

death rates stabilize at a low level.
5.  Fifth stage (proposed later) – Population decline
begins.

Set 50.q: 85. What is the meaning of the term 'Panplain'?

A nearly level surface created in the final
stage of river erosion
A plain formed due to human intervention

Set 51.q:
75. Which of the following statements is not
correct?
options:
The Eastern Jet Stream is found only in the
winter season.

The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
shifts maximum northward in June.

Monsoon winds exhibit seasonal reversal
patterns.

The Western Ghats receive rainfall mainly
from the Arabian Sea branch of the Indian
monsoon.
Set 51.explanation:
(a) : The Eastern Jet Stream is found only in the
winter season. This statement is incorrect.
In summer, the Western Jet Stream does not flow over
the Indian subcontinent, as the winds move northward
from the Tibetan plateau. During this time, the warm
Eastern Jet Stream influences the Indian subcontinent.
The primary reason for the formation of the warm
Eastern Jet Stream is the heating of the middle
atmosphere over the plateaus of Central Asia and Tibet,
creating a cyclonic circulation in a clockwise direction
in the middle troposphere. The heated air splits into two
separate streams:
(i)  The first stream moves toward the equator as the
Eastern Jet Stream.
(ii)  The second stream moves toward the North Pole as
the Western Jet Stream.
The Eastern Jet Stream moves southward over the
Arabian Sea, creating a high-pressure zone. Conversely,
the warm Jet Stream over the Indian subcontinent pulls
surface winds upward, forming a low-pressure system.
To fill this low-pressure area, winds from the high-
pressure Arabian Sea region move toward the northeast,
leading to the Southwest Monsoon.
The Western Ghats receive most of their rainfall from
the Arabian Sea branch of the Indian monsoon.
Monsoon winds change direction with the seasons. In
June, the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) shifts
maximum northward in the Northern Hemisphere.

22. The Koppen classification system focuses on

Set 52.explanation:
(a) : Koppen Climate Classification System–
1. Origin and Purpose –
• Developed by Wladimir Koppen, a German
climatologist in the world's climates based on average
temperature and precipitation.
• It links climate zones with natural vegetation,
assuming that vegetation is best expression of climate.
2.  Basis of Classification –
• Monthly average temperature
• Monthly average precipitation
• Annual trends in temperature and rainfall
3. Main Climate Groups (with codes) –
Code
Climate type

temperatures
year-

or

Cold winters and warm to
hot
summers;
large
temperature range
E

Very cold throughout the
year ; minimal precipitation
4. Subdivisions –
• Each group is further divided into subtypes based on
seasonal variations (like dry winter, wet summers,
etc.)
• f = no dry season (fully humid)
• S = dry summer
• w = dry winter
• a, b, c, d = Varying temperature levels (hot to cold)
Example –
Af = Tropical rainforest

Cfa = Humid subtropical

5. Features and uses –
• Scientific Importance : Helps understand climate
patterns and global distribution.
• Ecological Relevance : Closely related to types of
vegetation ecosystems.
• Practical Applications : Used in agriculture,
architecture, Urban planning and climate research.
6. Global relevance and limitations –
• Applied worldwide, supported with Koppen maps,
color-coded to show global climate zones.
• Doesn't consider wind, cloud cover, or extreme
weather events.

point is 30°×4 minutes = 120 minutes  = 2 hours

later i.e. at 7: 00 AM.

Set 53.q:
53. Which stage of demographic transition is
characterized by high birth rates and declining
death rates?
Set 53.explanation:
(b) : The second stage of demographic transition is
characterized by high birth rates and declining death
rates. In the early phase of this stage, fertility remains
high but gradually decreases over time, accompanying
the reduced mortality rate. In the first stage of
demographic transition, both fertility and mortality are
high, with little difference between them, resulting in a
nearly stable population. In the third stage, both fertility
and mortality decline, leading to a lower population
growth rate compared to the second stage. In the fourth
stage, both birth and death rates reach low levels and
stabilize, causing the population to stop growing and
remain stable.

following
stage
in
demographic transition model describes the
situation of high and stable birth rate along
with high and fluctuating death rate?
Set 53.explanation:
(c) : In the demographic transition model, the
highly stable phase describes a situation of high and
stable birth rate as well as high and fluctuating  death
rate. The demographic transition theory was originally
formulated by Thompson in 1929 and Notestein in
1945. Notestein and Thompson considered this theory
to have 3 stages, while Karl Sachs and trewartha
considered it to have 4 stages and Blacker and peter
Cox Considered to have 5 stages.
• According to the patterns arising from the mutually
changing relations between birth rate and death rate,
demographic transition is also valid for four stages.
1. High stationary stage - This is the first stage of
demographic transition in which the birth rate and
death rate are high and as a result of the gap being
less the population is almost stable.
2.  Early Expanding stage - This is the second stage of
demographic transition in which the birth rate
remains high and almost constant, but the death rate
starts declining, due to which the total population
gradually increases.
3. Late Expanding stage - In this third stage of
demographic transition, the birth rate also starts
declining and due to the sharp decline in death rate, it
reaches a low level, due to which population growth
becomes less than before.
4. Low stationary stage - This is the fourth stage of
demographic transition in which both birth rate and
death rate stabilize at a low level. Due to which
population growth almost stops.

Set 55.q:
44. A gradual change in population growth over a
long period is called:
Set 55.explanation:
(b) : A gradual change in population growth over
a long period is called demographic transition.
• The Demographic Transition Theory was first
proposed by Notestein in 1945.
Generally, there are five stages of demographic
transition:
1.  High stationary stage – Both birth and death
rates are high.
2.  Early expanding stage – Birth rate remains high,
but death rate declines.
3.  Late expanding stage – Both birth and death
rates decline, with a lower death rate.
4.  Low stationary stage – Birth and death rates
stabilize at a low level.
5.  Declining population stage – Birth rate falls
below the death rate.

Set 56.explanation:

11. Which
of
the
following
factors
is
not
responsible for the occurrence of temperature
inversion?
Set 56.explanation:
(c) : Generally, temperature decreases with
altitude, which is known as the "normal lapse rate of
temperature." However, in some cases, the situation
reverses, and the temperature starts increasing instead of
decreasing. This phenomenon is known as "temperature
inversion." Long, cloudless winter nights and calm
winds create ideal conditions for temperature inversion.
Therefore, strong winds are not responsible for causing
temperature inversion.

Concentration of carbon monoxide and
carbon dioxide

801
YCT

oxides

Concentration of carbon dioxide and sulfur
oxides
Set 56.explanation:
(c) : The main cause of acid rain is the
concentration of nitrogen oxides and sulfur oxides,
which are primarily released in industrial areas with
high levels of atmospheric pollution. These gases react
with oxygen to form H₂SO₄ (sulfuric acid), which then
mixes with water droplets in clouds, leading to acid
rain.

rain.

vertical air movement.

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not
explain (A).
Set 56.explanation:

Set 56.q:
23. What term describes the process by which ice
breaks off from a glacier and falls into the sea?
options: More than one of the above
Set 56.explanation:
(c) : Calving is also called glacier calving, which
means the breaking away of small icebergs. Generally,
when pieces of ice break off from the glacier terminus
and fall, it is called calving. Ice breaks from glaciers
because the moving glacier front becomes unstable.
Icebergs are formed as a result of this calving process.
Moraines, also known as glacial deposits, are formed
by the deposition carried out by flowing glaciers.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

Set 56.q:
90. Warm and cold-core rings are associated with
which oceanic phenomena?
Set 56.explanation:
(a) : Warm-core and cold-core rings are associated
with the Gulf Stream oceanic phenomenon. The Gulf
Stream was first discovered by Ponce de León. When
the Florida Current, after incorporating waters of the
Antilles Current, moves beyond Cape Hatteras, it is
known as the Gulf Stream. It is a wide and warm-water
current. On its right lies the Sargasso Sea, and on its
left, near the coast, lies a cold-water wall. Near the
coast, the water temperature ranges between 4°C to
10°C with lower salinity. Around 40°N latitude, the
Labrador Cold Current meets the Gulf Stream, causing
significant variations in its temperature and velocity.
This convergence of warm and cold currents generates
thermal inversion, resulting in dense fog near
Newfoundland, which obstructs navigation. The Gulf
Stream also raises the sea level along the eastern coast
of the United States.

Set 57.q: 12. Who introduced the term 'Pangaea'?
Set 57.explanation:
(a) : The 'Continental Drift Theory' was proposed
by the famous German climatologist and geologist
Alfred Wegener in 1912. However, its detailed
discussion took place in 1915 and 1920. Wegener
believed that during the Carboniferous period, all
landmasses were connected, forming a supercontinent
called Pangaea, which was surrounded by a vast ocean
named Panthalassa. The northern part of Pangaea was
called Laurasia, while the southern part was
Gondwanaland. Pangaea consisted of three layers:
Sial, Sima, and Nife. Over time, Pangaea broke apart,
forming the present-day continents and oceans.
Note: Pangaea began to break up in the Carboniferous
period, and Gondwanaland fragmented during the
Jurassic period.

Set 57.q:
14. Major environmental problems are infact the
manifestations of the degraded environments at
global level. These problems include:
A. Air and water pollution
B. Increase in the number of Wildlifes
C. Ozone layer depletion
D. Global warming
E. Climate change
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below
options: A, C, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
Set 57.explanation:
(a) : At the global level, the main environmental
problems include air and water pollution, ozone layer
depletion, global warming, and climate change. Air
pollution occurs when the level of pollutants in the air
exceeds safe limits and becomes harmful to humans,
animals, buildings, or any material. The main sources of
air pollution include, respectively: moving vehicles,
industries, construction sites and mines, fires, natural
processes and events (such as fireworks during festivals
and celebrations), etc.
Global warming refers to the increase in the Earth’s
average surface temperature, whereas climate change
means a long-term change in the climate of the Earth or
a part of it. Global warming only refers to the rise in
temperature, while climate change includes warming as
well as its harmful effects, such as the melting of
glaciers, heavy rainfall, storms, and recurring droughts.
The ozone layer is essential for life on Earth because it
absorbs most of the Sun’s harmful ultraviolet-B (UV-B)
radiation. When the ozone layer is depleted, UV-B
radiation reaches the Earth, causing problems such as
skin cancer, cataracts, climate change, etc. Therefore,
option (a) is correct.

increases and its height increases gradually.

Set 59.explanation:

its period remains constant, its speed decreases, and the

velocity; near the coast → lower velocity.
•  There is an inverse relationship between ocean depth
and tsunami wave height: shallower water → higher
waves.

and maximum height (~25 m) near continental coasts.

Set 59.q:
63. The book 'A New Soviet Heartland ' is related

Set 59.explanation:

associated with David J. M. Hooson. In the context of
the debate on the Rimland Model and its contemporary
relevance, Hooson, in 1964, through his book 'A New
Soviet Heartland', attempted not to add a new
dimension to the model but to redefine the central
area of the actual Heartland. Saul B. Cohen was the
first geographer who made a comprehensive attempt to
revise the Heartland–Rimland model. He presented his
views in his book 'Geography and Politics in a Divided
World' (1973). Halford Mackinder presented his

History') in 1904. Alexander P. de Seversky’s concept
of air power was mentioned in his book 'Victory
through Air Power' (1942).

percentage curve to graphically represent the inequality or

dioxide (CO2). The main greenhouse gases include

which of the following statements are correct.

B. The Southern part of mid-Atlantic Ridge is

C. The submarine ridge located between

Set 63.q:
88. Which of the following regions is not affected
by the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon?
Set 63.explanation:
(d) : The Punjab Plain is not influenced by the
Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon.
The Arabian Sea monsoon originates from the Arabian
Sea (Indian Ocean) and splits into three branches:
1.  Western Ghats Branch: Causes heavy rainfall
(>250 cm) in coastal areas. However, as it
descends beyond the Ghats, temperature rises, and
moisture decreases, leading to less rainfall in the
rain-shadow region (e.g., Bengaluru receives only
~50 cm rainfall).
2.  Narmada & Tapi Valley Branch: Travels inland
and causes moderate rainfall (e.g., Nagpur
receives ~60 cm).
3.  Aravalli-Himalayan Branch: Moves parallel to
the Aravalli Range and continues towards the
Himalayas, causing significant rainfall in the
northern regions.

Set 64.q: 5. What drives the movement of ocean currents?
options: More than one of the above
Set 64.explanation:
(d) : The movement of ocean currents is driven by
the Earth's rotation and winds. The Earth rotates on its
axis from west to east. Due to this motion, water cannot
keep up with the land and lags behind, resulting in the
generation of movement in the water from east to west.
Sometimes, some water also moves in the direction of
the Earth’s rotation, leading to the formation of counter-
equatorial currents. In addition, the Coriolis force,
differences in salinity, temperature variations, density
differences, air pressure, and winds also play important
roles in driving the movement of currents.

atmosphere system. Of the remaining 65 units, 14 are
absorbed by the atmosphere and 51 by the Earth’s
surface.
Therefore,
the
statement
claiming
the
atmosphere absorbs more than the Earth’s surface is
incorrect. Between 30° N latitude and the Arctic Circle,
incoming solar radiation is less than outgoing terrestrial
radiation, not more; thus the statement is incorrect. In
latitudinal heat transfer, atmospheric circulation is
stronger than oceanic circulation because atmospheric
circulation affects the ocean.

Set 64.q:
53. Which ecological cycle is directly driven by
sunlight?
options: More than one of the above
Set 64.explanation:
(d) : The cyclic flow of chemical elements
between living organisms and the environment in the
biosphere is called a biogeochemical cycle (ecological
cycle). This includes the water cycle, nitrogen cycle,
sulfur cycle, phosphorus cycle etc. These cycles are
primarily driven by solar heat. In an ecosystem, the
ultimate source of nitrogen is molecular nitrogen
present in the atmosphere, which cannot be directly
assimilated by plants and animals. Phosphorus is a
major component of biological membranes, nucleic
acids, and the cellular energy transfer system. In
ecosystems, the main input of phosphorus comes from
the weathering of phosphorus containing minerals in the
soil. Sulfur is an important component of proteins. It
occurs in both gaseous and sedimentary cycles.
Hence, more than or option is correct in the given
question, so option (d) is correct.

56. Which of the following concepts is most closely
associated with the spatial organisation of
urban systems in regional planning?
Set 64.explanation:
(a) : In regional planning, the central place theory
is most closely associated with the spatial organization
of urban systems. The central place theory seeks to
explain the regularity in the spacing of population
groups and settlements (inter-settlement distance) in a
region. In Berry’s words, “Central place theory is a
theory of the location, size, nature, spacing, and
function of central places.” The term central place was
first used in 1931 by Mark Jefferson. However, the
theory in its fully developed form was presented in
1933 by German geographer Walter Christaller. The
theory of urban land use development was presented by
Homer Hoyt in 1939.

Set 64.q:
68. Given below are two statements, one is labelled
as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Coastal odisha is highly cyclone
prone area of India.
Reason (R):  Mangrove trees do not get
uprooted by storms and tides because of there
extensive roots.

below:
Code-
options:

correct explanation of (A)

correct explanation of (A)
Set 64.explanation:
(a) : Coastal Odisha is the most cyclone-affected
region of India. The shape of India is peninsular, with
the Bay of Bengal on the east and the Arabian Sea on
the west. Therefore, the cyclones that occur here are
generated in these two water bodies. During the
monsoon season, cyclones are formed between 10° and
15° North latitudes. In the Bay of Bengal, most
cyclones originate between 16° and 21° North latitude
and west of 92° East longitude, but in July they arise
near the Sundarbans delta, around 18° North latitude
and west of 90° East longitude. Compared to the
Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal witnesses a greater
number of cyclones. Mangrove trees, because of their
widespread roots, are not uprooted by storms and tides,
and they reduce the impact of cyclones. Mangroves are
a type of vegetation whose roots remain submerged in
water. This vegetation is found in the delta regions of
the Ganga, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari,
Krishna, and Kaveri rivers.

•  The O-Horizon of soil comprises decomposable
organic matter like dried leaves, small rocks, fallen
trees and other organic debris.
•  The A Horizon predominantly comprises mineral
particles with minimal organic context.
•  The E Horizon representing a master Horizon
underlying other soil layers, is a subsurface horizon
characterized by severe leaching.
•  The B Horizon resides beneath the top soil and
serves as a reserved for water that has filtered
through the top layer.

Set 66.q: 14. Who introduced the term ‘Peneplain’?
Set 66.explanation:
(c) : The term Peneplain (nearly plain) was used
by W.M. Davis. He used this term in his concept of the
Geographical Cycle (1899). Among the plains formed
by river erosion, the peneplain is the earliest form. In
the final stage of their erosion cycle, rivers cut down the
elevated landmasses to their base level. The plain
formed in this manner is called a peneplain. However,
here and there, resistant rock outcrops remain, appearing
as small hills or low mounds. Such residual features are
called Monadnocks. Davis, in 1899, while presenting the
concept of the Geographical Cycle, explained that “a
geographical cycle is the period during which an uplifted
landmass, through the process of erosion, is transformed
into a featureless, nearly level plain.”

31. Arid conditions are caused by number of
factors like:
A. Global atmospheric circulation
B. Continentality
C. Warm offshore currents
D. Rain shadow effects
Choose the correct answer from the option
given below:
Set 66.explanation:
(d) : Dry conditions arise due to factors like
global atmospheric circulation, continentality, and
the rain-shadow effect. Under global atmospheric
circulation, descending air pressure in the tropical high-
pressure belt (e.g., Sahara, Thar) causes dryness.
Similarly, under continentality, regions located far from
the sea receive less humidity, leading to dry climates, as
in Central Asia. Under the rain-shadow effect, the
leeward slopes of mountains receive little rainfall,
causing dryness – for example, Ladakh, north of the
Himalayas. On the other hand, warm ocean currents
do not create dryness but instead increase humidity, as
they supply moisture to winds blowing across the sea
surf

Set 66.q:
74. What is the significance of the equatorial
region in terms of agriculture?
options:
Poor soil quality and not suitable for
agriculture
It has a diverse range of crops
More than one of the above
Set 66.explanation:
(b) : Poor soil quality, which is not suitable for
agriculture, is a characteristic of equatorial regions. This
is because in equatorial areas, high temperatures and
heavy rainfall lead to intense leaching of the soil.
During this leaching process, essential nutrients like
lime (Calcium Carbonate) and Silica are washed away
with rainwater, leaving behind soils rich in iron oxides
and aluminium compounds. The high temperatures also
promote rapid microbial activity, which quickly
decomposses organic matter and reduces the amount of
humus in the oil.
• As a result, the soils in equatorial regions are
generally not fertile enough for productive agriculture.
Extensive commerical farming is typically not practiced
in equatorial zones; instead, it is more option (b) is
correct, although the BPSC had marked option (c) is
correct answer.

surface.

rock heat at different rates, causing surface peeling.

Set 69.explanation:

such as the Rhône and Saône river valleys in France,
Southern Italy, Greece, Western Turkey, Syria, Israel,

America, Central Chile in South America, the

conditions. Therefore, cyclonic rainfall mostly occurs in
Europe and North America during winter.

Set 69.q:
24. As waves move toward the shore, their shape
undergoes
a
fundamental
transformation.
What is the correct sequence of these changes?
A. Short-interval crests
B. Wave breakers
C. Swash
D.  Backwash
Select the correct answer from the options
below:
options:
(A), (B), (C), (D)
NTA UGC NET/JRF Dec 2020/June 2021 Shift-II
Hydrosphere
358
YCT
Set 69.explanation:
(d) : As waves move toward the shore, they
undergo a fundamental transformation. The correct
sequence is: Short-interval crests → Wave breakers →
Swash → Backwash. Oceanic waves generally advance
toward the shore. As they approach the coast, the water
depth decreases. This causes the lower part of the wave
to rub against the seabed, slowing its forward
movement due to friction. As a result, the height of the
waves increases while their wavelength decreases.
When the wave crest becomes too high, it collapses
forward and moves toward the shore. This broken water
wave is called surf, breaker, or swash. When the water
retreats from the shore, it is called backwash.

environment (place) determines the livelihood patterns

Set 69.q:
79. Who emphasized the thermal influence of the

Set 69.explanation:

Plateau, which rises 5 km into the atmosphere, absorbs
more solar radiation and heats up significantly during
summer. This creates a thermal anticyclone above it,
weakening the western subtropical jet stream south of
the Himalayas while forming an eastern jet stream.
Initially, this jet stream emerges over eastern India but
later shifts westward, extending over India, the Arabian
Sea, and East Africa. This process strengthens the high-
pressure system over the Indian Ocean, leading to the
onset of the southwest monsoon.

Set 70.q:
11. Which ocean current transports warm water
from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic
Ocean to Western Europe, affecting its climate?
options: More than one of the above
Set 70.explanation:
(c) : The Gulf Stream current carries warm water
from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic Ocean to
Western Europe, thereby influencing the climate there.
Near 45° N latitude and 45° W longitude, the Gulf
Stream splits into several branches, collectively called
the North Atlantic Current. One branch flows along the
coast of Norway (Western Europe) into the Norwegian
Sea; another, known as the Irminger Current, moves
toward the southern coast of Iceland; and a third flows
toward the eastern coast of Greenland. The Gulf Stream
significantly affects the climate along the eastern coast
of North America and the coastal regions of
northwestern Europe. In these areas, the temperature is
about 4°F higher than the average temperature for their
latitudes. Due to the Gulf Stream, a temperate climate
develops in Western Europe, which is why its ports
remain ice-free throughout the year despite being
located in high latitudes.

Set 71.q: 1. Who introduced the term "Geography"?
Set 71.explanation:
(c) : The term "Geography" was first used by
Eratosthenes in Greece. He attempted to establish
geography as a distinct field of study. Eratosthenes
divided the known Earth into five zones: one torrid
zone, two temperate zones, and two frigid zones.
He was the first scholar to use a gnomon to measure the
correct length of the equator and estimated the Earth's
circumference to be 25,000 miles (actual: 25,860 miles).
In his book, he referred to the habitable world as
"Oikoumene." He also attempted to measure the
distances of the Sun and Moon from the Earth.
Other Greek scholars who contributed significantly to
geographical knowledge include Thales, Anaximander,
Hecataeus, Aristotle, Theophrastus, Polybius, and
Posidonius.
